# x86_64 Relocation Survey — LINK.EXE grounding (vms-680)

**Generated by `tools/survey_x86_64_relocs.sh` — do not hand-edit.**
Re-run the script to regenerate; `tools/survey_x86_64_relocs.sh --check`
(wired into CI) diffs a fresh run against this file and reds if it drifts.

## Method

Cross-compiled every non-test `.c` file in the vms-b65.1-.6 object set
(`src/vmsprocess`, `src/libvms`, `src/vmsfs`, `src/vmslnm`, `src/vmsrms`,
`src/vmsdcl`) to x86_64 `.o` files with:

```
musl-gcc -fPIC -O2 -mtls-dialect=gnu2 -c -I<component>/include ...
```

(`-fPIC -mtls-dialect=gnu2`, per vms-be5's standing precedent for x86_64
OVMX builds — see `src/imgact/test/run_test_x86_64.sh`.) Every produced
`.o` was scanned with `readelf -r` and every distinct `r_type` name was
tallied by occurrence count across the whole object set.

Files that failed to compile standalone (missing kernel/system headers
outside this tree, multi-TU-only symbols, etc.) are excluded from the
tally and listed below for transparency — they contribute no relocation
data either way.

## Cross-reference: LINK.EXE's existing R_AARCH64_* switch

`src/vmslink/link.c`'s relocation-apply switch (~lines 615-990) currently
handles only `R_AARCH64_*` types. Mapping observed `R_X86_64_*` types to
their ARM64 analog (or noting no analog exists) is the input the
downstream x86_64 reloc-apply items (vms-8f5, vms-cd1, vms-2e4) implement
against:

Table covers only the r_type values the run above actually observed —
no type is listed unless it appears in the tally with a nonzero count.

| R_X86_64_* (observed) | R_AARCH64_* analog in link.c | notes |
|---|---|---|
| R_X86_64_64 | R_AARCH64_ABS64 | direct analog — absolute 64-bit address, S+A |
| R_X86_64_PC32 | R_AARCH64_PREL32 (partial) | 32-bit PC-relative, S+A-P; x86_64's workhorse call/jmp/lea-rip disp32 has no single ARM64 analog (ARM64 splits this across ADRP+ADD/LDR page-relocs) |
| R_X86_64_PLT32 | R_AARCH64_CALL26 / JUMP26 (role analog only) | PC-relative PLT-routed call; ARM64's CALL26/JUMP26 play the equivalent linker role via a different encoding (26-bit imm vs 32-bit disp) |
| R_X86_64_GOTPCREL | R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE + LD64_GOT_LO12_NC (role analog only) | PC-relative GOT-entry load; ARM64 splits GOT access across two page/offset relocs, x86_64 does it in one PC32-class reloc |
| R_X86_64_REX_GOTPCRELX | (no ARM64 analog) | x86_64 linker-relaxation variant of GOTPCREL (mov->lea when GOT slot provably unneeded); ARM64 has no equivalent relaxable-GOT-load reloc class |
| R_X86_64_GOTPC32_TLSDESC | R_AARCH64_TLSDESC_ADR_PAGE21 (role analog only) | TLSDESC GOT-slot address computation (PC-relative GOT offset, first half of the x86_64 TLSDESC codegen pair); ARM64's ADR_PAGE21 plays the equivalent role via a page/offset split instead of a flat PC32 |
| R_X86_64_TLSDESC_CALL | R_AARCH64_TLSDESC_CALL | direct analog — same TLSDESC model, project standardizes on `-mtls-dialect=gnu2` specifically to land here (2-reloc x86_64 GOTPC32_TLSDESC+TLSDESC_CALL pair) instead of the TLSGD/GD model `-mtls-dialect=gnu` (the default) would emit |
| R_X86_64_DTPOFF32 | (no ARM64 analog observed in link.c) | module-relative offset of a TLS variable within its TLS block, filled as an absolute 32-bit constant and added to the TLSDESC resolver's returned TP-offset at runtime (observed: paired 1:1 with each __thread variable reference, immediately following a GOTPC32_TLSDESC/TLSDESC_CALL pair); ARM64's TLSDESC path encodes the equivalent module offset inside the GOT-slot resolver data itself (via TLSDESC_LD64_LO12/ADD_LO12), not as a separate static .o-file reloc against the operand |

## Cross-reference: LINK.EXE (static, in .o files) vs IMGACT.EXE (load-time)

`src/imgact/imgact.c`'s x86_64 arch handling (vms-913.11, arch/x86_64/) is
LOAD-time: it walks the shareable image's `DT_RELA`/`DT_JMPREL` dynamic
relocation tables at activation and applies `R_X86_64_RELATIVE`,
`R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT`, `R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT`, and `R_X86_64_TLSDESC` — the
*dynamic* reloc set that exists because the image is a real ET_DYN ELF
shareable being loaded into a process.

None of `R_X86_64_RELATIVE`, `GLOB_DAT`, or `JUMP_SLOT` appear in the
static `.o`-file survey above — they are synthesized by the *linker*
(GNU ld today; OVMX's own LINK.EXE going forward) when it builds the
`.dynamic`/GOT/PLT sections, not emitted by the compiler into object
files. `R_X86_64_TLSDESC` is the one type that appears in BOTH: as a
static `.o`-file reloc (compiler-emitted, link-time — LINK.EXE's job) AND
as a load-time `DT_RELA` entry pointing at the TLSDESC GOT slot
(IMGACT's job) — LINK.EXE resolves the compile-time TLSDESC relocation
into a GOT-slot-producing form, and IMGACT resolves that GOT slot's
dynamic entry at activation. The two jobs are sequential stages on the
same symbol, not overlapping responsibility for the same event.

**Confirmed: LINK.EXE's job (this survey) and IMGACT's job (load-time
DT_* relocs, already handled per vms-913.11) are not the same set.**
